auth_methods.quote: You should prefer the OAuth 2.0 flow if building an app for multiple workspaces. If you are building an app for a single workspace, you can manually generate an API key to make requests on behalf of that workspace only.

oauth_scopes_documented.quote: Both OAuth access tokens and single-workspace access tokens use scopes to control the resources that the token has access to and the actions that can be performed on those resources.

access_model.quote: Apps in Attio's App Store and access to Attio's API are available on all Attio plans.

access_notes.value: API access is available on all Attio plans, including the self-serve Free plan (up to three users). A single-workspace API key can be generated in developer settings; OAuth apps are built in the developer console at build.attio.com. To get tokens for other workspaces, an app must be shared with those workspaces or published.
access_notes.quote: Apps in Attio's App Store and access to Attio's API are available on all Attio plans.

official_mcp_server.quote: For other MCP clients: Add `https://mcp.attio.com/mcp` as a remote MCP server and complete the OAuth authentication when prompted.

rate_limits.value: 100 requests per second for read requests; 25 requests per second for write requests; score-based limits on List records and List entries endpoints with a 10-second sliding window
rate_limits.quote: Our rate limit across the whole API is 100 requests per second for read requests, 25 requests per second for write requests.

webhooks.quote: Setting up and listening to webhooks

verdict_reason: Attio publishes a public REST API with an OpenAPI specification, OAuth 2.0 and self-serve API keys, documented scopes, webhooks, and explicit rate limits. API access is available on every plan including the free self-serve tier, so a developer can obtain credentials without sales contact or approval. Attio also operates a hosted MCP server at mcp.attio.com/mcp.
